 Sixers Face Bucks and Pistons in Weekend Back-to-Back After 29-Point Comeback
 ✓ 
 By 
 Vince Carey 
 Sports Reporter 
 Published 
 October 23, 2026 
 3 min read 
 Share 
 𝕏 
 f 
 Make us a preferred source 
 The Sixers host the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday and the Detroit Pistons on Sunday, both at 7:30 p.m. at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Joel Embiid said he will play in only one of the two games, Philadelphia basketball reporter Austin Krell posted on X. The Sixers are 2-0 after the largest comeback in team history in the play-by-play era.
 Embiid plans to play one of the two, per report
 Embiid said he would play one of the two weekend games, Philadelphia basketball reporter Austin Krell posted late Thursday night, Heavy reported . The report did not say which game he will sit. The team has not announced a plan, and neither team had submitted its official NBA injury report for Saturday’s game as of the league’s 9 a.m. Friday update.
 There has been no report that LeBron James will rest either night. Both stars played between 33 and 35 minutes in each of the first two games.
 Depth at center is thin. Ariel Hukporti, signed to back up Embiid, tore his right Achilles in the preseason and is out for the season ( our report ). Adem Bona, back from a foot sprain, and Jabari Walker are the options behind Embiid.
 A 29-point comeback against Cleveland
 The Sixers trailed Cleveland by 29 points on Thursday and won 114-106 in their home opener. “The 29-point comeback was the Cavaliers’ largest blown lead and the Sixers’ largest comeback in the play-by-play era,” ESPN reported . It was also the largest comeback of James’ career.
 Tyrese Maxey scored 32 points, Embiid added 24 and Jaylen Brown 21, with 10 of his in the fourth quarter. James had 17 points, 10 rebounds and three steals, according to the Basketball Reference box score . The Sixers opened the season with a 106-100 win at the Knicks on Tuesday, when Maxey scored 28 ( our home opener preview ).
 Saturday: Bucks on the second night of a back-to-back
 Milwaukee arrives without Giannis Antetokounmpo, whom it traded to the Miami Heat with Bobby Portis in a deal that brought back Tyler Herro, Fox6 reported . The Bucks, under first-year coach Taylor Jenkins, lost their opener 128-116 at Washington on Wednesday, when Herro had 24 points and nine assists. They host Chicago in their home opener at 4 p.m. on Friday, a game moved up to avoid the World Series opener, so Saturday is the second night of a back-to-back for them.
 Sunday: a rested Pistons team
 Detroit plays at Miami at 8 p.m. on Friday and has Saturday off. The Pistons opened with a 121-113 win over Boston, rallying from a 22-point second-half deficit with a 23-0 run, NBA.com reported . Cade Cunningham had 22 points and eight assists and Jalen Duren added 22 for coach J.B. Bickerstaff.
 How to watch Sixers vs. Bucks and Pistons
 Saturday vs. Milwaukee, 7:30 p.m.: NBC Sports Philadelphia, plus NBA TV nationally
 Sunday vs. Detroit, 7:30 p.m.: NBC Sports Philadelphia
 After the weekend, the Sixers visit Indiana on Wednesday at 7 p.m., then play a second back-to-back: the Knicks at home on Friday, Oct. 30, and Charlotte on the road on Saturday, Oct. 31.
